**Claim.** For all $s \in S$: $(f \vee g)(s) = \tfrac12\big(f(s) + g(s) + |f(s) - g(s)|\big)$. Hence, as mappings $S \to \R$, $f \vee g = \tfrac12\,(f + g + |f - g|)$.

**Unpacking the right-hand side.** By the definitions of pointwise addition, pointwise difference, absolute value of a real-valued function, and pointwise scalar multiplication, the mapping $h := \tfrac12\,(f+g+|f-g|)$ is defined on $S$ with values in $\R$ by
$$h(s) = \tfrac12\big((f+g)(s) + |f-g|(s)\big) = \tfrac12\big(f(s) + g(s) + |(f-g)(s)|\big) = \tfrac12\big(f(s) + g(s) + |f(s) - g(s)|\big)$$
for every $s \in S$. Both $f \vee g$ and $h$ are mappings with domain $S$ and codomain $\R$, so they are equal if and only if they agree at every $s \in S$.

**Lemma.** For all real numbers $a, b$: $\max\{a,b\} = \tfrac12\,(a + b + |a - b|)$.

*Proof of Lemma.* Since $\le$ is a total order on $\R$, either $a \ge b$ or $a < b$.

- Case $a \ge b$. Then $a - b \ge 0$, so $|a-b| = a - b$ by definition of absolute value. Hence $\tfrac12(a + b + |a-b|) = \tfrac12(a + b + a - b) = \tfrac12 (2a) = a$. Also $\max\{a,b\} = a$, since $a \in \{a,b\}$ and $a \ge b$, $a \ge a$, i.e. $a$ is the greatest element of $\{a,b\}$. (This includes the case $a=b$, where $\{a,b\}=\{a\}$ and $\max\{a\}=a$.)

- Case $a < b$. Then $a - b < 0$, so $|a-b| = -(a-b) = b - a$. Hence $\tfrac12(a + b + |a-b|) = \tfrac12(a + b + b - a) = \tfrac12(2b) = b$. Also $\max\{a,b\} = b$, since $b \in \{a,b\}$, $b > a$ and $b \ge b$.

In both cases the identity holds. $\blacksquare$

**Proof of the Claim.** Let $s \in S$ be arbitrary. Put $a = f(s)$ and $b = g(s)$, which are real numbers since $f, g$ are real-valued. By definition of the pointwise maximum and the Lemma,
$$(f \vee g)(s) = \max\{f(s), g(s)\} = \tfrac12\big(f(s) + g(s) + |f(s) - g(s)|\big) = h(s).$$
Since $s$ was arbitrary, $f \vee g$ and $h$ agree at every point of their common domain $S$, and both have codomain $\R$. Therefore
$$f \vee g = \tfrac12\,\big(f + g + |f - g|\big). \qquad \blacksquare$$
